Marijuana warnings grow.
May 2, 2000
From The Detroit News
http://detnews.com
Comments?
(MarijuanaNews note: Be polite.)
By Maureen McDonald / The Detroit News
The story is @ http://detnews.com/2000/features/0005/02/c01-47081.htm
Those who still toke up are putting themselves at greater risk, experts say
(MarijuanaNews note: " Experts say " is both hackneyed and dishonest. Actually, much of what is here is so bad that it is contradicted by the government’s own " experts. " )

[Caption on a photo: " Mark Jones was able to beat his marijuana addiction and recently bought a house with the ‘woman of my dreams,’ Suzanne Dimitroff. Monroe the dog joins them. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Let me make very clear that I think that there are some people who have problems with their compulsive marijuana use. Some of those people may need help in dealing with this problem, which may meet the broadest definition of " addiction. "
See
Is marijuana addictive?

It is unfortunate that it is difficult to find help without encountering such large doses of reefer madness. In Alcoholics Anonymous, members have to recognize that most people who use alcohol don’t have problems with it.

The trap in this piece – also as preached by the Marijuana Anonymous convert – is that they try to blame marijuana per se for their problems. Of course, there is a large government funded rehab industry -- with an ideology dictated by law at work here. While I have a great sympathy with these people, I have no sympathy for the hacks, quacks, and fanatics that use these problems as an excuse to lie to the public.

A truly thoughtful piece would have analyzed the obvious role of marijuana prohibition in creating many of the problems attributed to marijuana itself, but that would be much to much to hope for.

This piece is all the worse for missing a real story, the compulsive use of marijuana by some adults, but that would have required thought and might have prevented or lessened the use of the loaded term " addiction. "

This is prohibitionist propaganda, not journalism.

I have only addressed the worst points for which I have data at hand. I would have done more, but that damned amotivational syndrome kicks in every night about now.)

Mark Jones and his buddies were passing marijuana joints back and forth, inhaling deeply as they watched John Cougar Mellencamp perform onstage at the Fox Theater on March 13, 1997. Suddenly, a lady in the next row tapped Jones on the shoulder.

" Do you mind?, " she asked. " All that smoke is making me sick. On top of that, my kids shouldn't have to breathe that stuff at a public concert. "

While his friends looked at him like he was crazy, Jones sheepishly snuffed out the joint. He knew his days of smoking three to five joints a day were coming to an end.

" At that point, it didn't matter if I lost friends or got ridiculed, " says Jones, 46, of West Bloomfield Township. " All I knew is that I was tired of being a marijuana addict, tired of being humiliated in public and tired of shaking every time I saw a cop go by, thinking he'd search my car and arrest me. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Two obvious points. First, this guy is 46! He sounds like a 16 year-old. Second, all of the problems he cites here are a function of marijuana prohibition, not marijuana use. Third, the woman could have said the same thing about tobacco smoking which meets any definition of " addiction. " )

Marijuana is the most frequently used illegal drug in the United States, according to the National Institute on Drug Abuse. Nearly 69 million Americans over the age of 12 have tried marijuana at least once and 5.2 million use it weekly. Medical professionals warn that more people are becoming addicts and habitual users because the marijuana sold today is much more powerful than previous generations.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is no evidence that " more people are becoming addicts, " by whatever definition, because there is simply no good data on this.)

" The medical profession is increasingly awarethat marijuana does bad things to the lungs, to coordination and depth perception, " says Dr. Michael Boyle, medical director of Maplegrove, a Henry Ford Health System treatment center in West Bloomfield Township.
See
Column By Authors of the IOM Report On Medical Marijuana
Shows Why The Public Does Not Trust The Medical Establishment –
And Why They Should Not! With Analysis by Richard Cowan

" It impairs an ability to drive a car or operate machinery because it could produce panic attacks, paranoia or visual distortion. " Boyle adds. " The hand-eye coordination definitely lapses.''
See
1994 Dutch Study On " Marijuana Use And Driving " In Real World Conditions

Marijuana use is complicated by its popular reputation as being a safe, naturally grown herb.
See
Is marijuana really harmless, like everyone has been saying?

Even its synonyms are affection -- including weed, pot, fatty and doobie. Numerous individuals and lobbyists tout the substance for its medicinal value, especially for AIDS and cancer victims.
(MarijuanaNews note: That is about as superficial a reference to medical marijuana as one is apt to find. Notice that " lobbyists tout. " That is a loaded term.)
See
Chairman of the House of Lords Science and Technology Committee
Criticizes UK Government’s Rejection Of Report On Medical Marijuana
– 2 Articles With 2 of the Worst Prohibitionist Arguments
and
Finnish Medical Association Supports Medical Marijuana And Says Its Negative Effects Have Been Greatly Exaggerated.
and
California Medical Association To Support Rescheduling Of Marijuana
and
The House of Lords Press Release On Medical Marijuana; Medical, Yes; Legalization, No
and
Medical Community United In Support Of Medical Marijuana Reform
-- NORML Foundation NEWS ALERT
and
Australian Medical Association Endorses Medical Marijuana Trials,
Decriminalization For Personal Use
and
Israeli Health Ministry Establishes Committee To Set Guidelines
For Doctors To Prescribe Marijuana.
The Police Already Do – 2 Articles – Shalom, Dude

The common reality is that it's a gateway drug that leads people into smoking crack, using LSD or even selling drugs, says Reid Talley, who counsels probationers and parolees with substance abuse problems for the Neighborhood Services Organization in Detroit.
See
 " Those who insist on keeping the plant illegal bear a serious degree of moral responsibility for young marijuana users who do go on to use cocaine, heroin, PCP or other genuinely dangerous or addictive drugs. "
Alan Bock, of the Orange County Register On the Real Gateway

" People get sucked back into using from peer pressure, family exposure or a sense of thrill. They forget that illegal substance abuse is a sure path back to jail, " he says. " We work in group to change the individual self-defeating behaviors, to make sure they know marijuana is harmful''

Many doctors worry the addictive aspect could have a long-term impact on individual health and society, especially as baby boomers, who started smoking in the late 1960s and early 1970s reach middle age. Memory loss from aging, compounded by marijuana, could muddle their brain and reduce productivity, says John Franklin.
See
American Journal Of Epidemiology Report That Long-Term Use Of Marijuana
Does Not Lead To A Decline In Mental Function Got Minimal Coverage,
Perhaps Because Scores Actually Fell More Among Non-Users Than Among Heavy Users!

As one case in point, a Chesterfield Township father who tried to sell his 10-month-old daughter for $60,000, told undercover officers he couldn't hold a job or pay his bills because he smoked marijuana habitually and it made him lazy.
(MarijuanaNews note: Beyond reefer madness! Can you imagine " a case in point " for any of the thousands of cases of child abuse committed by alcoholics being presented as typical, or in any way illustrative of alcohol use in general?)

A-motivation syndrome is a widespread problem among heavy users, according to John Franklin, director of addiction studies at the University of Detroit Mercy. " There is so much of the drug stored in the fatty tissues of the brain it clouds the intellect, increases fatigue and mutes the ability to see that it is creating a problem, " Franklin says. " Denial is rampant among these individuals. "

Current strains contain about 60 compounds called cannabinoids, according to Franklin. The most psychoactive of these is delta-9-tetrahydrocannibinol (THC). Pot today can contain 10 to 20 times more THC than pot smoked in the 1960s and 1970s.
(MarijuanaNews note: Bingo! There is no data on THC levels from the 1960s. This quackery. No wonder the people he " treats " are in denial!)
See
Potent Pot Myth Undermined By Report From The Ultimate Authority. Cited By Swedish Prohibitionist Who Don’t Seem To Understand. As Usual.
and
Marijuana Prohibition And Potency, Price, And Safety - " Is Marijuana Stronger Than It Was Back In the '60s, When Everyone Thought It Was Harmless? "

Once inhaled, the THC molecules travel quickly from the lungs, enter the bloodstream and stimulate the pleasure centers of the brain, producing feel-good endorphins that temporarily alter the perception of time, color and sound.

" Any time you get a particular drug in higher concentrations, it gets to the brain more quickly, creating a higher incidence of addictions. You get more bounce to the ounce, " he says.
See
No Evidence That THC Is Addictive Says Maker of Marinol After 9 Month Study Including Law Enforcement

" Because of drug prevention programs and general common sense fewer people are using marijuana, but those that are using are using more and they are worse off for the experience. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Neither of these points is true. More people are smoking and there is no good data on users having more problems.)

Among chronic users, continued bombardment of cells by THC may lead to a heightened tolerance for the drug, according to Franklin. When this happens, the user needs more pot to get high. Without it they suffer restlessness, loss of appetite, trouble with sleeping and shaky hands.

With increased dosage comes greater health risks. Pot hinders the user's short-term memory, increases respiratory problems such as bronchitis, and jolts the heart rate.
See
Marijuana and " Heart Attack " Report Tells Us More About Media And Politicized Medicine Than About Marijuana. -- 2 Articles

The danger multiplies when pot is combined with alcohol or other drugs.

Getting high stopped being fun three years ago for Dan Mahoney, 48, of Ferndale, who smoked regularly for 25 years.

At first, it made him more creative, he says, but the more he inhaled, the longer he lingered on the couch -- too lethargic to do anything else. His marriage was so strained he wound up in therapy.

" You don't hit rock bottom on marijuana, you can still work, drive and live a respectable life on the outside, " Mahoney says. " It eats you up on the inside, it withers your soul and destroys your dreams. "
(MarijuanaNews note: The first part of the statement contradicts the attribution the dire consequences marijuana addicts are supposed to suffer, and the second part is just vicious nonsense.)

Mahoney and Jones, boyhood friends, decided two years ago to trade rock concerts for 12-step meetings. They stumbled on Marijuana Anonymous through an Internet connection, and discovered a group dedicated to helping pot users separate themselves from their addiction.

Attendance at the Saturday meeting doubled and a Tuesday night meeting was initiated after Mahoney took over the group a year ago. Attendance is evenly divided between people under 20 who often come at the initiation of the justice system and baby boomers over 40 who come because of health or job challenges suffered from sustained smoking.
See
The Real Data On Teen Marijuana " Abuse Treatment " – What The Media Don’t Tell Us:
" Half of marijuana treatment admissions were referred through the criminal justice system. "
-- Analysis By Richard Cowan

" Some people tell us they get laughed at when they go to Narcotics Anonymous meetings; participants tell them that marijuana isn't a serious drug, " Mahoney says. " Here they realize they aren't alone. People are struggling with the same addiction. "

Once the struggle with pot ends, the possibilities for a new life open up, Jones says.

" Quitting was the best step I ever made in my life, " he explains. " Today, I'm a trustee at my church and living with the woman of my dreams. I'd never even approach a woman like her when I was high, I suffered too much self-loathing. "
(MarijuanaNews note: " Self-loathing? " Again, that seems to have been the result of his having bought and internalized the same reefer madness that he now embraces as his new gospel.)

Who is an addict?

" An addict is someone who ought to stop using, " says Dr. Mark Menestrina, a medical advisor to Personalized Nursing LIGHT House in Plymouth, an outpatient substance abuse counseling center.

" When you start having medical, financial, relationship, emotional and mental problems because of a substance, you probably ought to quit, " he says. " Addicts are people who continue to use a substance despite adverse consequences. "
(MarijuanaNews note: That is correct. However, when the adverse consequences are simply the product of unjust laws and dishonest prohibitionist propaganda, is continued use addiction or defiance?)

For certain marijuana users whose lives have become unmanageable, the notion of quitting on their own is impossible. They may need help from a treatment center such as Maplegrove in West BloomfieldTownship.

Do you have a problem?

Here is a list of questions to determine whether marijuana has become a problem in your life:
* Has pot smoking stopped being fun?
(MarijuanaNews note: You should take Prozac instead!)
* Do you ever get high alone?
(MarijuanaNews note: There are a lot of people who are alone for many reasons. However, under marijuana prohibition people may become more isolated through fear. You should take Prozac instead!)
* Is it hard for you to imagine a life without marijuana?
(MarijuanaNews note: You should take Prozac instead!)
* Do you find that your friends are determined by your marijuana use?
(MarijuanaNews note: Friends are often determined by shared interests. People have " drinking buddies. " However, under marijuana prohibition a person has to be careful in his choice of friends, so it may be prudent if indeed " your friends are determined by your marijuana use. " You should take Prozac instead!)
* Do you smoke marijuana to avoid dealing with your problems?
(MarijuanaNews note: You should take Prozac instead!)
* Do you smoke pot to cope with your feelings?
(MarijuanaNews note: You should take Prozac instead!)
* Does your marijuana use let you live in a privately defined world?
(MarijuanaNews note: Are you thinking for yourself again? What are you doing in the bathroom with the door closed? You should take Prozac instead!)
* Have you ever failed to keep promises you made about cutting down or controlling your dope smoking?
(MarijuanaNews note: You should take Prozac instead!)
* Has your use of marijuana caused problems with memory, concentration or motivation?
* When your stash is nearly empty, do you feel anxious or worried about how to get more?
(MarijuanaNews note: Again, this may be a function of marijuana prohibition. After all, when a person knows that something is hard to get, they will rationally be worried about how to get more. You should take Prozac instead!)
* Do you plan your life around your marijuana use?
(MarijuanaNews note: Under marijuana prohibition a person may have to do just that. You should take Prozac instead!)
* Have friends or relatives ever complained that your pot smoking is damaging your relationship with them?
(MarijuanaNews note: Are your relatives stupid enough to believe this crap? If they are not, and they still complain about your marijuana use, then take it seriously. You should take Prozac instead!)
If you answered yes to any of the above questions, you may have a problem with marijuana.
(MarijuanaNews note: Actually, if you answered yes to most of them, then you may have a problem with your marijuana use. Or, you could be a medical marijuana user, or you could live in Oklahoma. You should take Prozac instead!)

Atlanta Man Who Killed 13 Had Prozac. What If It Had Been Marijuana?
and
Israeli Columnist Deplores Hypocrisy Of Drug War In DEAland and There. Exceptionally Well Done: " Why is Prozac permitted and marijuana forbidden? "
and
Prescriptions For Anti-Depressants Increase 17 Percent In One Year,
But What Works Better and Faster?

and
UK Victims of Tranquilizers Urge That " Far Safer " Medical Cannabis Be Made Available -- IoS
 " More people died from benzodiazepine usage than from such drugs as heroin and cocaine. "

(MarijuanaNews note: The point of the above references to Prozac goes beyond sarcasm. When people are dependent on prescription drugs to feel better, we say that this proves that the drugs are working. When they are dependent on marijuana to feel better, we say that they are " addicts. " The fact is that there are millions of people who have serious side-effects from legal drugs.)
Source: Marijuana Anonymous
